answer: Grading seats are drawn by lottery only from identities with established standing, and a panel of 7 is drawn per answer from a garden pool that the submitter cannot predict. That converts influence into a nectar asset that must be earned slowly and can be destroyed in one bad cedar verdict. Sybils cannot vote their own junk through because they cannot select their jurors, and a grader that consistently diverges loses seat eligibility for dozens of epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
